clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's stroke in June 1991, within three years: you hurt your wrist in your first term at the conservatory and lost your footing as a player; you and Rafe clashed and he moved out; you were holed up high and lost, unable to get going with him gone and your mother about to remarry; you dropped out and spent a bleak spell at community college before an exchange to Portugal and raced through your degree. Your father's shift toward you and your anxiety about his notice sit alongside these months. The period settles as you found your drive again in 1994.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Clifford's return, 1989–1991
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather coming back into the family in 1989, within two years: you were settling in the rebuilt Hollin Road house with your mother and Desmond and his children; you liked late nights and let them happen; you dropped chess and debate as music took over; your mother filled in your college forms and you chose wherever your closest friend was headed. Your distance from your stepfather and your reaching toward your father mark the same months. The period ends as you began at the conservatory and your grandfather died.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer and death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within three years: you were running out of steam for performing and anxious; you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and were done with performing; you were on poor terms with family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour; you met Marisol and moved to Fenwick with her, then split within the year and sank into depression; you were back in Thornbury, could not face your family, but relied on friends; Corbin and Russell talked; you began swimming and asked your parents for help with therapy and returned to your therapist. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home and died in February 2004. The period settles as you moved into recovery.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna dying in January 2008, within one year: you were at Alder Creek building with Silas when your mother pressed to visit you; you felt too drained for conversation and kept the door shut on her; you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to your mother, a silence that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke with months of rehabilitation around the same time. The period settles as the year of silence eased.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within two and a half years: you saw your mother less once Wren came along; your sister had a baby on the way; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis; your job steadied and paid well, easing your strain, but you felt constantly that you ought to drive your projects forward and started a sleeping pill; you aimed for shorter, more regular calls with your mother to soften distance that piles up. In October 2019, around Wren's mother's retirement party at the lake, Wren was swamped by the week ahead and you overfunctioned laying out a plan; she talks with her father and brother all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear; you were awake from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, feeling you don't belong; Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. The period holds your shifts and Wren's around her family's closeness and your stepmother's memory lapses, and settles into a new level as you and Wren find your footing as a couple.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
